meta.title_en: Nursing Practice in Oman: OMSB, Scope, Documentation & Patient Rights
meta.source_note: Content references publicly available Oman MOH and OMSB documentation. All local norms require verification by a nurse licensed in Oman before use in generation.

lay_summary: This module covers the regulatory framework for nurses working in Oman under the Oman Medical Specialty Board (OMSB) and the Ministry of Health Oman, including scope of practice, patient rights, documentation requirements, and infection control relevant to the OMSB nursing licensing exam.

lessons.title: OMSB and Oman MOH: Nursing Registration and Scope of Practice

content.intro: Nursing practice in Oman is regulated by the Oman Medical Specialty Board (OMSB) and the Ministry of Health (MOH) Oman. All nurses wishing to practise in Oman must obtain Oman MOH registration and pass the OMSB Prometric licensing examination.

sections.heading: Nurse Registration in Oman
sections.text: Nurses in Oman register with the Ministry of Health Oman's Directorate General of Nursing Affairs. The OMSB administers the Prometric licensing examination that all foreign-trained nurses must pass. Oman MOH classifies nurses as: Registered Nurse (diploma or BSN), Senior Nurse, Specialist Nurse, and Nurse Consultant. Registration requires: verified academic credentials, good standing certificate from home country, passing the OMSB licensing exam, and a valid certificate of good health.

sections.heading: Scope of Practice in Oman
sections.text: Standard RN scope in Oman includes: patient assessment and care planning, medication administration per physician order, patient and family education, wound care and dressing, vital signs monitoring, and documentation. Prescribing medications is not within the standard RN scope — a physician order is required for all medications. Advanced practice nurses (specialist/consultant) may have extended competencies in defined clinical areas per MOH approval. Oman's healthcare system is primarily delivered through MOH hospitals and polyclinics, supplemented by Royal Hospital (tertiary referral) and private facilities.

sections.heading: OMSB Prometric Exam Overview
sections.text: The OMSB nursing exam is a computer-based Prometric examination of 150 MCQ questions completed in 3 hours. Blueprint topics: Medical-Surgical Nursing, Maternal and Child Health, Psychiatric and Mental Health Nursing, Paediatric Nursing, Community Health, Nursing Fundamentals, Leadership and Management. The passing threshold is set by OMSB and varies by cohort. Source: OMSB official candidate handbook.

content.clinical_pearl: OMSB exam questions on delegation and scope of practice are common. Oman follows the international standard: the nurse who is delegating retains accountability for the outcome. Only tasks within the competency of the delegatee may be delegated — assessment cannot be delegated to an unregistered care assistant.
key_points: Oman MOH registration required before practising
Standard RN scope: assessment, medication administration (per order), education
Prescribing: physician order always required for standard RN
Delegation: nurse retains accountability; assessment cannot be delegated

lessons.title: Patient Rights, Consent, and Incident Reporting in Oman

content.intro: Oman's legal framework for patient rights and healthcare practitioner responsibilities is governed by the Law of the Practice of Human Medicine (Royal Decree 75/2009) and Oman MOH policies. Understanding these is essential for the OMSB exam.

sections.heading: Patient Rights in Oman
sections.text: Oman MOH Patient Rights Charter guarantees: the right to receive care without discrimination, the right to information about diagnosis and treatment in an understandable manner, the right to give or refuse informed consent, the right to privacy and confidentiality, the right to access medical records, and the right to lodge a complaint. In Oman, patient information must be communicated in Arabic or in the patient's language with translation assistance. The nurse is responsible for ensuring the patient understands the information provided.

sections.heading: Informed Consent in Oman
sections.text: Oman follows the principle that a legally competent adult patient must provide informed consent before any procedure or treatment. Consent must be documented in the medical record with the patient's signature. For emergency situations where the patient is unable to consent and no guardian is present, emergency care may proceed in the patient's best interest. For minors (under 18) and incapacitated adults, a legal guardian or next of kin provides consent. Nurses must ensure the patient has received sufficient information to make an informed decision and that consent is voluntary — not obtained under duress.

sections.heading: Incident Reporting in Oman
sections.text: Oman MOH mandates incident reporting for all adverse events, near-misses, and sentinel events. Hospitals use internal incident reporting systems. Sentinel events must be escalated to hospital management and reported to Oman MOH as required. Nurses must complete an incident report promptly following any adverse event, including patient falls, medication errors, and equipment failures. Documentation of the incident in the medical record is also required — separately from the incident report (which is an internal quality tool and NOT part of the legal medical record in most Oman MOH facilities).

content.clinical_pearl: A key OMSB exam concept: the incident report is NOT part of the patient's medical record — it is an internal quality improvement tool. The nurse must document the facts of what happened in the medical record separately. Never reference the incident report in the medical record entry.
key_points: Competent adults: right to consent or refuse treatment
Emergency exception: care may proceed without consent if patient incapacitated and no guardian present
Incident report is NOT part of the medical record — document facts separately in chart
Sentinel events: report to Oman MOH

lessons.title: Medication Safety, Infection Control, and Regional Diseases in Oman

content.intro: Medication safety in Oman follows Oman MOH pharmacy standards and international best practice. Regional diseases relevant to Oman's nursing exam include MERS-CoV and tropical infections. All lab values use SI units.

sections.heading: Medication Safety in Oman
sections.text: Oman MOH medication safety standards require: two-patient identifier check before every administration, five rights verification (patient, drug, dose, route, time), independent dual-nurse verification for high-alert medications (concentrated electrolytes, insulin, heparin, opioids), accurate controlled drug register with dual witness signatures. Drug names in Oman use INN (International Nonproprietary Names/generic names): paracetamol (not Tylenol), ibuprofen (not Advil), metoclopramide (not Reglan). Lab units: glucose mmol/L, creatinine µmol/L, potassium mmol/L, temperature °C.

sections.heading: Infection Control: Oman Context
sections.text: Oman MOH follows WHO and GCC infection control standards. MERS-CoV is regionally significant: apply Standard + Droplet + Contact Precautions, N95 for aerosol-generating procedures, report to Oman MOH mandatory. Brucellosis is relevant in Oman due to cattle and camel exposure — patients presenting with fever, sweats, and joint pain after animal contact should prompt consideration. Dengue fever cases occur in Oman, particularly in Dhofar governorate. Standard hand hygiene follows WHO 5 Moments. Oman participates in GCC-wide infection surveillance.

sections.heading: Occupational Safety for Nurses in Oman
sections.text: Oman MOH facilities follow occupational health standards for healthcare workers: hepatitis B vaccination is mandatory for all clinical staff, annual TB screening is required, and needlestick injury protocols must be followed immediately (wash, report to occupational health, initiate post-exposure protocol as indicated). Personal protective equipment must be used per facility policy based on transmission-based precaution levels. Nurses have the right to report unsafe working conditions through facility occupational safety channels.

content.clinical_pearl: OMSB questions on regional diseases often involve MERS-CoV precautions or Brucellosis presentation. MERS: standard + droplet + contact. Brucellosis: think undulant fever + joint pain + animal or unpasteurised dairy contact. Lab confirmation by serology (Brucella agglutination test). Treatment: combination antibiotics (doxycycline + rifampicin typically).
key_points: Drug names: generic (INN) — paracetamol not Tylenol, ibuprofen not Advil
Labs: SI units — glucose mmol/L, creatinine µmol/L
MERS-CoV: standard + droplet + contact + report to MOH
Brucellosis: undulant fever + joint pain + animal exposure

flashcards.question: Which body administers the Prometric nursing licensing exam in Oman?
flashcards.answer: OMSB — Oman Medical Specialty Board. All foreign-trained nurses must pass the OMSB Prometric exam before practising in Oman.

flashcards.question: How many questions are on the OMSB Prometric nursing exam?
flashcards.answer: 150 MCQ questions in 3 hours (computer-based Prometric format). The passing threshold is set by OMSB and varies by cohort.

flashcards.question: With which Ministry do nurses register to practise in Oman?
flashcards.answer: The Directorate General of Nursing Affairs within the Oman Ministry of Health (MOH). Both MOH registration and passing the OMSB exam are required.

flashcards.question: What OMSB exam principle applies to nursing delegation?
flashcards.answer: The nurse who delegates retains accountability for the outcome. Assessment cannot be delegated to an unregistered care assistant — only tasks within the delegatee's competence may be assigned.

flashcards.question: What is the key rule about the incident report and the medical record in Oman?
flashcards.answer: The incident report is NOT part of the patient's legal medical record — it is an internal quality improvement tool. Clinical facts must be documented separately in the chart without referencing the incident report.

flashcards.question: What regional disease should Oman nurses consider in a patient presenting with undulant fever, joint pain, and animal contact?
flashcards.answer: Brucellosis. Lab confirmation by Brucella agglutination test. Treatment typically includes doxycycline + rifampicin. Distinct from MERS-CoV presentation.

flashcards.question: What precautions apply to a suspected MERS-CoV patient in Oman?
flashcards.answer: Standard + Droplet + Contact Precautions. N95 for aerosol-generating procedures. Mandatory reporting to Oman MOH.

flashcards.question: What are the high-alert medications requiring dual-nurse independent verification in Oman?
flashcards.answer: Concentrated electrolytes (e.g., potassium chloride), insulin, heparin, and opioids. Both nurses verify two patient identifiers plus all medication details.

flashcards.question: What occupational health measure is mandatory for all clinical nurses in Oman MOH facilities?
flashcards.answer: Hepatitis B vaccination is mandatory for all clinical staff. Annual TB screening is also required. Needlestick injuries require immediate washing, reporting to occupational health, and initiating PEP.

flashcards.question: What generic names should be used for common medications in the Oman context?
flashcards.answer: INN generic names: paracetamol (not Tylenol), ibuprofen (not Advil), metoclopramide (not Reglan). All lab values use SI units: glucose mmol/L, creatinine µmol/L, temperature °C.

mcq_questions.question: The OMSB (Oman Medical Specialty Board) Prometric nursing licensing exam consists of:

options.C: 100 MCQ questions plus a practical OSCE

mcq_questions.explanation: The OMSB nursing exam is a computer-based Prometric exam of 150 MCQ questions completed in 3 hours. The passing threshold is set by OMSB and varies by cohort. Source: OMSB Candidate Handbook.

mcq_questions.question: A Registered Nurse in Oman wishes to independently prescribe paracetamol for a patient with mild pain. Is this within standard RN scope under Oman MOH?

options.A: Yes — paracetamol is an over-the-counter drug and nurses may prescribe it
options.B: Yes — prescribing is within RN scope for non-controlled medications
options.C: No — prescribing is not within standard RN scope; a physician order is required
options.D: Yes — after 3 years of experience, Oman RNs may prescribe selected drugs

mcq_questions.explanation: In Oman, prescribing medications is not within the standard RN scope of practice. A physician order is required for all medications. Only Specialist/Consultant Nurses may have extended competencies in defined areas with specific MOH approval.

mcq_questions.question: Following an adverse patient event (unexpected fall with injury) in an Oman MOH hospital, how should the nurse document this?

options.A: Write a detailed incident report and include a copy in the patient's medical record
options.B: Document the clinical facts (what happened, assessment, interventions, outcome) in the patient's medical record AND complete a separate internal incident report; do not reference the incident report in the chart
options.C: Notify the MOH directly and await further instructions before documenting
options.D: Document only in the incident report — the medical record entry is optional

mcq_questions.explanation: Oman MOH requires that the incident report (an internal quality tool) is kept separate from the patient's medical record. The nurse must document clinical facts in the chart AND complete the incident report. The incident report is NOT part of the legal medical record and must never be referenced in the chart entry.

mcq_questions.question: A nurse in Oman is delegating a task to an unregistered care assistant. Which task is appropriate to delegate?

options.A: Performing an initial patient assessment on a newly admitted patient
options.B: Monitoring vital signs on a stable patient (collection, not interpretation)
options.C: Administering oral medications per physician order
options.D: Deciding whether a patient is ready for ambulation

mcq_questions.explanation: Vital sign collection (not interpretation or clinical decision-making) is within the competence of an unregistered care assistant. Assessment, medication administration, and clinical judgements are within RN scope and cannot be delegated to unlicensed personnel. The delegating nurse retains accountability for the outcome.

mcq_questions.question: A patient in Oman presents with 3 weeks of intermittent fever, night sweats, joint pain, and a history of working with camels on a farm. Which condition should the nurse prioritise in the assessment?

options.A: MERS-CoV — initiate droplet and contact precautions immediately
options.B: Brucellosis — a regionally significant zoonosis associated with animal contact
options.C: Dengue fever — confirm travel history to Dhofar
options.D: Malaria — arrange thick blood film immediately

mcq_questions.explanation: Brucellosis (undulant fever) is endemic in Oman and the GCC. Presentation: prolonged intermittent fever, night sweats, and joint pain in a patient with animal (camel, cattle) or unpasteurised dairy contact. Confirmed by Brucella agglutination test. Treatment typically includes doxycycline + rifampicin. MERS-CoV would also involve respiratory symptoms.

mcq_questions.question: What is the required precaution level for a confirmed MERS-CoV patient in an Oman hospital?
mcq_questions.explanation: Oman MOH guidelines follow WHO and GCC standards for MERS-CoV: Standard + Droplet + Contact precautions. An N95 respirator is required for aerosol-generating procedures (not a surgical mask). Reporting to Oman MOH is mandatory. Negative pressure room should be used if available.

mcq_questions.question: An Oman MOH nurse sustains a needlestick injury while recapping a needle. What is the immediate correct action?

options.A: Apply pressure to squeeze out blood from the wound to remove contamination
options.B: Wash the wound immediately with soap and water, report to occupational health, and initiate post-exposure protocol
options.C: Apply a sterile dressing and continue working — report at end of shift
options.D: Suck the wound to remove any blood contamination

mcq_questions.explanation: Oman MOH occupational safety protocol for needlestick injury: immediately wash the wound with soap and water (do NOT squeeze or suck), report promptly to occupational health, and initiate post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) as indicated per facility protocol. Document in an incident report.

mcq_questions.question: A patient in Oman who is incapacitated following a road traffic accident requires emergency surgery. No family member is immediately available. What is the correct approach to consent?

options.A: Postpone surgery until a family member is contacted and provides consent
options.B: Proceed with emergency surgery in the patient's best interest and document the emergency exception clearly in the medical record
options.C: Transfer the patient to another facility where consent can be obtained
options.D: Obtain telephone consent from the nearest family member

mcq_questions.explanation: Oman's legal framework allows emergency care to proceed without consent when the patient is incapacitated and no guardian is immediately present, provided it is in the patient's best interest. The emergency exception and rationale must be documented clearly in the medical record.

mcq_questions.question: Which vaccination is mandatory for all clinical nursing staff in Oman MOH facilities?
mcq_questions.explanation: Oman MOH occupational health standards mandate hepatitis B vaccination for all clinical healthcare staff. Annual TB screening is also required. These are mandatory occupational health requirements, not optional.

mcq_questions.question: A nurse in Oman administers insulin to the wrong patient due to a patient identification failure. What is the correct sequence of actions?

options.A: Notify the physician, complete incident report, correct the documentation to show the intended patient
options.B: Assess the patient for hypoglycaemia → notify the physician immediately → document accurately in the chart → complete the incident report
options.C: Complete the incident report first, then notify the physician
options.D: Notify the family first, then involve the physician

mcq_questions.explanation: The standard sequence for medication errors in Oman: first assess the patient for immediate harm (insulin error → risk of hypoglycaemia), then notify the physician immediately, document clinical facts accurately in the medical record, and complete a separate internal incident report. Never alter or falsify documentation.

mcq_questions.question: A nurse in Oman documents a patient's blood glucose reading. Which unit is correct?
mcq_questions.explanation: Oman and all GCC countries use SI units. Blood glucose is reported in mmol/L (not mg/dL, which is used in the United States). Creatinine is µmol/L; temperature is in °C; potassium is mmol/L.

mcq_questions.question: What legal framework governs medical practice and healthcare practitioner responsibilities in Oman?

options.B: Oman Royal Decree 75/2009 — Law of the Practice of Human Medicine

mcq_questions.explanation: The primary legal framework for healthcare practice in Oman is Royal Decree 75/2009 — the Law of the Practice of Human Medicine. This establishes the rights and responsibilities of healthcare practitioners, including informed consent and patient rights obligations.
